subject: history
title: Containment and Crisis Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace how the Cold War turned hot in Korea and froze Europe in two.
meta_desc: GCSE History — Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, Berlin Blockade, NATO and Korean War.
final_note: You learned how containment, the Berlin Airlift, NATO and Korea cemented the Cold War divide.

walkthroughs.body_html:
In March 1947 Truman promised to help any country fighting communism.

This Truman Doctrine was followed by the Marshall Plan — about $13 billion of aid for Western Europe. Stalin saw it as American interference and forbade Eastern bloc countries from taking it.

In June 1948 Stalin cut land routes into West Berlin.

The West responded with the Berlin Airlift — flying in food and fuel for 11 months. Stalin lifted the blockade in May 1949. West Germany (FRG) and East Germany (GDR) were created soon after.

NATO was formed in April 1949 — 12 Western nations promising mutual defence.

In June 1950 communist North Korea invaded the South. A UN force led by the USA fought back. The Korean War ended in 1953 with the border roughly back where it began.
